transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-10-28
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Kapur (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Redwood Solutions), Ellen Park (Solarflare Head of Platform), Marcus Li (SRE), Priya Nair (Security), Diego Ramos (ML Eng)

Summary:
Ellen and team are evaluating Redwood for low-latency customer-facing classification + summarization features embedded in their network management console. They want to understand integration options (SDKs, LangChain / LlamaIndex connectors), gateway/proxy setup, rate limits & quotas, and observability hooks. Heavy focus on security: VPC/private deployment, KMS, audit logs, SSO. Agreed to run a benchmark pilot and share pricing + security pack.

Topics:
- Integration approach: hosted API vs dedicated vs private (VPC/on-prem)
- SDKs and LangChain / LlamaIndex examples
- Gateway / proxy patterns and egress controls
- Rate limits, quotas, burst policies and throttling behaviors
- Observability hooks: tracing, token-level cost breakdown, per-route metrics
- Security: SOC 2, KMS, SSO, audit logs, RBAC

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood, and with me is Ravi our solutions engineer and Jordan on solutions. How are you all?
[00:08] Ellen Park: Hi Maya, hi Ravi, thanks. We're excited - we've been evaluating a few vendors and wanted to dig into integration questions.
[00:14] Marcus Li: Yeah hi, Marcus here. Mostly SRE questions today, traffic profiles, quotas, that kind of thing.
[00:18] Maya Chen: Awesome. Quick agenda - we'll do a short intro, then Ravi can walk through integration patterns, SDKs, LangChain and LlamaIndex, and then open up for security and ops. Sound good?
[00:27] Priya Nair: Sounds good.

[01:12] Ravi Kapur: Thanks. So at a high level Redwood provides three main deployment modes - hosted API, Dedicated (reserved GPU pools), and Private/VPC or on-prem if you need full network isolation. For integrations there are three common approaches: direct SDK/REST calls from app servers, a local gateway/proxy that sits in your VPC and forwards to Redwood (useful for firewall rules and egress control), or an on-prem inference deployment for air-gapped needs.
[01:48] Diego Ramos: Quick Q on the SDKs - do you have official python/js SDKs and do they support streaming and function calling?
[01:56] Ravi Kapur: Yes official SDKs for Python and Node; they support streaming, tool-calling and structured outputs. There's also pre-built connectors for LangChain and LlamaIndex - we have examples in the repo. Sometimes the naming in the docs is slightly off, but we keep the samples up to date.
[02:12] Ellen Park: Can you share a LangChain example? We use a mix of LangChain in our MLE pipelines and LlamaIndex for vector stores.
[02:18] Ravi Kapur: Absolutely - we have a LangChain LLM wrapper and a LlamaIndex retriever example that uses Redwood embeddings. We can share a sample repo; the typical pattern is to use Redwood's embedding endpoint for indexing and then the generation endpoint for responses.

[03:00] Marcus Li: On traffic - our console sees bursts during rollouts and incident windows. Typical baseline is ~40 qps, burst up to 400 qps for short periods. P95 latency requirements are sub-250ms for classification calls, open to higher for longer summarization flows. How do you handle burst capacity and throttling?
[03:20] Ravi Kapur: Good question. For Hosted we have quota and rate-limits per API key with burst tokens; Dedicated gives you reserved throughput and predictable P95s. We also have burst capacity options and autoscaling policies - for Dedicated you can configure buffer instances that warm up to handle spikes. For Hosted, our rate limits are enforced at the gateway and we have token bucket behavior with configurable per-tenant quotas.
[03:48] Maya Chen: If you're sensitive to throttles during incidents we usually recommend Dedicated or Private so you control capacity. Hosted is good for quick testing and smaller workloads.

[05:05] Priya Nair: Security - we need KMS integration (customer-managed keys), audit logs for all request/response metadata, and SSO with SAML. Also data residency - some telemetry must stay in EU. Do you support that?
[05:20] Ravi Kapur: Yes on Private/VPC you can integrate your KMS/HSM, and we support customer-managed keys. Audit logs and request-level tracing can be shipped to your SIEM or to Redwood console depending on deployment. We support SAML/SSO and RBAC for user roles. For hosted customers we have region choices and data residency options per contract; for strict requirements private deployment is recommended.
[05:54] Ellen Park: How do you redact or avoid storing sensitive PII in logs?
[06:00] Ravi Kapur: We can configure redaction at the gateway level and mask tokens in logs. For Private deployments you can opt-out of any telemetry leaving the VPC.

[06:32] Diego Ramos: On latency, what's the typical end-to-end for short classification models (~2-4k tokens) on Hosted vs Dedicated?
[06:40] Ravi Kapur: Hosted for small models typically 80-200ms depending on region and model. Dedicated can be tuned for consistent sub-100ms p95 if you reserve capacity and use model variants we recommend. Note: quantization and kernel choices affect numbers.
[06:58] Marcus Li: Are there observability hooks - distributed tracing, per-route metrics, token-level cost? We want to attribute cost to product features and trace a request from frontend to tokenization to model inference.
[07:10] Jordan Lee: Yes - Redwood Console exposes per-route/model dashboards, token-level cost breakdowns, and tracing hooks that integrate with OpenTelemetry. You can attach trace ids in headers and see the end-to-end latency split (queueing, network, model time). We also export metrics to Prometheus and logs to your SIEM.

[08:12] Ellen Park: On the gateway/proxy pattern - we want to place a lightweight proxy in front of Redwood so we can control egress and implement additional auth. Any recommended patterns?
[08:22] Ravi Kapur: Recommended is an internal gateway that handles auth, per-route rate limiting, and request normalization. For LangChain and LlamaIndex connectors you'd call the gateway which then forwards to Redwood. We have examples using Envoy and nginx plus a small Node/Go shim that adds trace headers and handles key rotation.
[08:44] Priya Nair: Do you support mutual TLS to Redwood and IP allowlist?
[08:48] Ravi Kapur: For Private and Dedicated yes. Hosted supports IP allowlist per enterprise contract and mTLS can be configured for private peering.

[10:15] Ellen Park: Costing - we need an idea of unit economics. For embeddings vs generation what's typical? Also we want to compare hosted per-token vs Dedicated monthly commit.
[10:28] Maya Chen: We'll send a pricing sheet but high-level: hosted is per-token (and per-embedding unit); dedicated is a reserved monthly commit with lower per-token equivalent cost and predictable throughput. There's also cost for data egress and observability retention if you pick long-term retention. We'll include example TCO scenarios in the pricing sheet.

[12:05] Diego Ramos: On LlamaIndex integration - any special config for vector store sizes, sharding or retrieval latency considerations?
[12:14] Ravi Kapur: For vector stores we recommend smaller chunk sizes for better retrieval recall; embeddings throughput is parallelizable. Retrieval latency depends on vector store (FAISS, Milvus) and we recommend async prefetch and caching of top-k candidates. We also have a reranker endpoint to reduce token cost by filtering candidates.

[14:00] Marcus Li: For our pilot we want to test: classification (short) at 100 qps sustained, and summarization load (longer) at 20 qps. Can you support running a short benchmark with sample prompts and measuring p95 and cost per request?
[14:14] Ravi Kapur: Yes - we'll put together a benchmark plan. Ravi: I'll propose test harness, sample prompts, and a runbook. We can run Hosted tests quickly; Dedicated pilot requires provisioning but we can simulate with a dedicated sandbox.

[15:30] Priya Nair: Auditing - we need a clear list of what you're logging, retention windows, and ability to turn off request content logging.
[15:42] Maya Chen: We'll include that in the security pack - default logs, retention, and controls for redaction or disabling content storage.

[17:05] Ellen Park: Any gotchas with LangChain and streaming? We rely on streaming to the UI to show partial summarization.
[17:12] Ravi Kapur: We support streaming via SDKs and the LangChain wrapper. One gotcha: if you use gateway buffering you need to forward streaming chunks properly (chunked transfer). We have a recommended pattern in the example repo.

[18:40] Diego Ramos: If we use LlamaIndex + embeddings, can we pin a model version for reproducibility?
[18:46] Ravi Kapur: Yes - you can pin model versions and pin quantization profiles. For Dedicated and Private you get tighter control over kernel selection and quantization to ensure stable outputs.

[20:00] Marcus Li: Network peering - for Private do you provide a private endpoint in our VPC or do we host entirely?
[20:08] Jordan Lee: For VPC deployment we provide a private control plane and data plane in your VPC - sometimes we do a customer-managed data plane. If fully on-prem, we provide an appliance or container package. We'll map options in the security pack.

[22:30] Ellen Park: What's the SLA for Dedicated? Uptime and latency SLOs?
[22:36] Maya Chen: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets depending on the capacity tier; we'll include the SLA terms in the enterprise proposal.

[24:00] Priya Nair: For compliance we need SOC 2 Type II, ISO certs, and ability to pass security questionnaires.
[24:08] Maya Chen: We'll attach SOC 2 and ISO docs; we also have a security questionnaire pack that covers common vendor assessments.

[26:15] Diego Ramos: On caching and prefix KV cache - you mentioned KV cache earlier. How does that work for multi-turn context?
[26:24] Ravi Kapur: KV cache is used for autoregressive decoding to avoid recomputing prefixes; we also support prefix caching across requests for identical contexts. For multi-turn you can reuse KV caches to reduce token compute. We expose controls for cache TTLs and invalidation.

[28:00] Ellen Park: Any limitations with models and quantization when using LlamaIndex? Some libraries expect fp16 outputs.
[28:10] Ravi Kapur: Quantization can change numeric behavior; we recommend testing evals for regressions. Redwood Optimize gives suggestions on quantization profiles by workload, and quality regression alerts tied to prompt sets.

[30:22] Marcus Li: Are there audit logs for admin actions in the console? We need RBAC and admin audit trail.
[30:29] Jordan Lee: Yes - RBAC, SSO, and admin audit logs are available; we'll show examples in the security pack.

[32:00] Ellen Park: On rate limits, can we set per-route or per-feature quotas so that internal tooling can't starve customer-facing flows?
[32:09] Ravi Kapur: Yes - per-route and per-key quotas are supported. You can create policies that prioritize production routes, and set fallback policies to lower-cost model variants if capacity thresholds are hit.

[34:00] Diego Ramos: For the developer experience, what does the SDK error handling look like? We want graceful retries and idempotency keys for requests.
[34:08] Ravi Kapur: SDKs include retry helpers, idempotency token support, and structured error codes. We recommend exponential backoff and using idempotency for mutating ops.

[36:50] Priya Nair: Data retention for embeddings - do you store them by default? Can we opt out?
[36:58] Maya Chen: Embeddings can be stored or not depending on your contract. For Privacy-first customers we can disable retention or keep them encrypted with customer-managed keys.

[38:20] Marcus Li: Operationally, during a rollout if we see model regressions, can you do canary and A/B rollouts?
[38:28] Jordan Lee: Yes built-in support for canary deploys, A/B tests, and automatic fallback policies. You can run percentage-based rollouts and compare metrics in the console.

[40:05] Ellen Park: Ok this is great. For the pilot what do you need from us?
[40:10] Ravi Kapur: We'll need a traffic profile (qps, payload sizes), representative prompts, and a list of success criteria (p95 latency, cost per request, quality metrics). Marcus you mentioned those - if you can share.
[40:22] Marcus Li: Yep we'll put together a spreadsheet and send it.

[42:00] Maya Chen: Recap - Maya to send pricing and security pack; Ravi to send benchmark plan and LangChain/LlamaIndex sample repo; Solarflare to share traffic and SLOs. Align on pilot dates next week.

[43:15] Ellen Park: One last question on legal - do you support standard data processing addendums and customer-friendly IP clauses?
[43:25] Maya Chen: We have standard DPAs and can negotiate enterprise terms; legal can follow up after we send the SOW.

[45:00] Diego Ramos: Quick integration note - we'll likely put a proxy in our VPC that handles auth and rate-limiting, then forward to Redwood depending on whether we pick Hosted or Dedicated.

[45:12] Ravi Kapur: That pattern works well. We'll include an Envoy example and a minimal Node shim in the repo.

[47:40] Priya Nair: Can you also include an example of setting up OpenTelemetry headers so traces show up in our Jaeger?
[47:50] Jordan Lee: Yep we'll include trace header examples and an OTEL config snippet.

[49:30] Maya Chen: Great. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up via email with the attachments and propose times for the tech deep-dive.
[49:40] Ellen Park: Thanks Maya, Ravi - appreciate it.
[49:45] Marcus Li: Thanks.
[49:48] (call ends)

Notes on transcript quality: automated transcription had occasional mis-hear of product names ("Redwood Dedicated" -> "Redwood decide"), and some speaker label swaps early in the call. Natural speech fillers and small overlaps present.
